contract_review: Exercises the Cadastre downloader with fake network streams and real temporary cache files: canonical URL, freshness and strict sidecars, gzip/SHA verification, failed-refresh preservation, atomic pair rollback, persistent recovery evidence and simulated link/junction fail-before-network controls.

review_notes: Read the temporary cache sidecar, set its timestamp to current UTC minus the supplied timedelta, and rewrite JSON so freshness scenarios are controlled without waiting.

Recompute size and SHA256 from the temporary archive and rewrite those sidecar fields; the corruption test deliberately makes metadata consistent with bad gzip bytes to isolate decompression validation.
Assert the exact official latest commune-31395 parcel archive URL.
Replace network opening with BytesIO gzip payload, run real temporary publication, and assert output bytes/identity/size/cache_hit plus schema-1 sidecar commune/timestamp.
Call twice with one fake stream and assert the opener ran once, second cache_hit=True and identical SHA/timestamp.
Age a valid sidecar by 169 hours, supply refreshed gzip bytes and assert two opener calls, cache miss, exact replacement bytes and their independently computed SHA.
Age the cache, simulate HTTPError on refresh and assert archive bytes survive plus the sidecar file still exists; this test does not assert exact sidecar-byte equality.
Simulate HTTPError on first acquisition and require controlled error with an empty temporary cache directory.
Compare returned archive SHA256 with hashlib.sha256 over the exact fake-network payload.
Write the gzip fixture and assert the private decompression validator returns true.
Write the fixture with its final eight bytes removed and assert gzip validation returns false.
Replace cached bytes with truncated gzip and update sidecar size/SHA to match those bytes; assert decompression failure still forces a second fake request and refreshed bytes.
Expire the cache, return truncated gzip on refresh, and assert controlled error leaves original archive bytes and no .part files.
Assert uppercase 2A004 and 2B033 produce their corresponding two-character department/commune/filename URL suffixes.
Reject integer, lowercase Corsican, surrounding-whitespace and alphabetic commune examples with TypeError/ValueError naming commune code.
Reject six timeout inputs: zero, negative, NaN, infinity, numeric text and bool.
Reject five age inputs: negative, NaN, infinity, numeric text and bool.
Forge size mismatch, wrong SHA or invalid timestamp separately and assert a second opener call returns refreshed archive bytes.
Reject bool/float schema and bool/float/text size metadata through cache miss, evidenced by two opener calls and cache_hit=False.
Write a timestamp one hour in the future and assert refresh with exact new bytes.
Replace the sidecar with duplicate-key JSON, nonstandard NaN JSON or an array root and assert all three cases refresh rather than return a hit.
Fail only temporary-sidecar replacement during refresh, then assert exact original archive/sidecar bytes and absence of .part/.bak leftovers.
Raise OSError for the precise temporary-metadata-to-final-metadata replacement; delegate all other filesystem replacements to the captured real helper.
Simulate sidecar publication failure on first acquisition and assert neither final artifact nor .part/.bak leftovers remain.
Raise for the exact first sidecar publication replacement; otherwise call the original file replacement helper.
Fail metadata publication plus selected archive or metadata rollback and require a rollback error with at least one useful backup remaining; this test checks existence, not backup contents.
Raise at metadata publication and the selected backup-restoration source, otherwise perform the real replacement.
Create a real stale archive backup, then assert a subsequent call rejects before its opener sentinel and preserves both backup and final archive bytes.
Cause publication/archive-rollback failure, assert both backups contain old bytes, then retry with a forbidden-network sentinel and require recovery rejection without changing either backup.
Fail precise metadata publication and archive-backup restoration operations; delegate unrelated replacements.

Across archive/metadata temporary paths and symlink/junction kinds, monkeypatch link detection plus path-open redirection to a sentinel; require zero fake-network calls and unchanged sentinel bytes. These are simulated links, not native link creation.
Report the selected unsafe path as a symlink for the symlink case, otherwise delegate to captured Path.is_symlink.
Report the selected unsafe path as a junction for the junction case, otherwise delegate to captured Path.is_junction.

Redirect attempted opens of the unsafe temporary path to the real sentinel, preserving mode/options; otherwise open the real requested path. This sentinel would expose accidental writes through a link.
Increment the closed-over fake-network call counter and return BytesIO; the test expects this callback never to run.
Simulate a symlink at a missing backup path and require recovery rejection before the network sentinel.
Report the recovery path as a link even when it does not exist, otherwise use the original filesystem link check.
Increment the closed-over counter then always raise AssertionError; its annotated BytesIO return is never reached.
Combine metadata publication, archive rollback and subsequent temporary cleanup failures; assert the controlled error still names rollback and both backups retain exact original bytes.
Raise at publication, then set the closed-over rollback_failed flag and raise at archive restoration; delegate all other replacements.
After rollback has failed, raise PermissionError only for temporary metadata cleanup; otherwise delegate to captured Path.unlink.
